source.title: The Dynamics of Learning: A Random Matrix Approach

record.file_problem: Full paper text and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes training and held-out classification error over training time in a linear classifier on natural Gaussian-mixture data, and validates theoretical predictions with simulations and MNIST. This conceptually bears on V1's natural-label generalization, but it does not test random-label memorization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training and generalization error over time, simulations, and MNIST validation. Its discussion of dropout, weight decay, stochastic gradient descent, and minibatch size is background or future-work context, not tested results. It does not test arbitrary-label fitting or the claim versions about width, convolutional architecture, adaptive optimizers, large batches, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes early stopping and generalization dynamics in a linear classifier, but tests none of V1–V8. Natural-label accuracy alone does not test V1's coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization. Varying the input-dimension/sample-size ratio does not test V2's hidden-layer width claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive asymptotically deterministic training and generalization dynamics for a full-batch, squared-loss linear classifier on Gaussian-mixture data, explain conditions favoring early stopping, and report close agreement with simulations on modified binary MNIST data.
record.recipe_differences: Single-layer linear classifier, squared loss, full-batch gradient descent, and Gaussian-mixture data; MNIST validation uses two classes with whitening and added noise. V1 specifies larger networks and random-label fitting.
record.method_sensitivity: Training time: generalization error rises slightly after an initial drop while training error continues toward zero. The authors state that overfitting becomes more severe as the training sample size approaches the data dimension; the displayed c = 1 case is described as ending at 0.5.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gaussian-mixture data, generalization error initially falls and then rises slightly while training error continues toward zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early stopping can improve held-out performance relative to converged least-squares training in a high-dimensional linear classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical training and generalization trajectories closely match simulations on whitened, recentered MNIST digits 1 and 7 with added Gaussian noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The random-matrix approximation predicts learning dynamics in this modified binary MNIST setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 predicts chance-level limiting classification at p/n = 1, whereas Section 5.3 finds no overtraining as p/n approaches zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization cost of converged least-squares training depends on the input-dimension/sample-size ratio.

record.problems: The principal analysis is for a single-layer linear classifier with a Gaussian-mixture model, squared loss, and full-batch gradient descent. The MNIST validation uses only digits 1 and 7, a selected training set of n = 784, and artificial Gaussian noise. The text gives no uncertainty estimates for these experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result meeting the row criteria was left out. Theoretical discussion of optimizer, regularization, and minibatch effects is not an experiment in this study.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level held-out performance on random labels, and coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Hidden-layer widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover accuracy.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Dropout and large-batch generalization appear as background or future research, without corresponding comparisons. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Tests generalization on natural labels and the training-versus-test error trajectory. Does not train on random labels or compare the same recipe's natural-label and random-label performance.

rows.subject: single-layer linear network
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on two-class Gaussian-mixture data; training and generalization misclassification rates over training time.

conditions.value: Gaussian mixture with means ±µ; µ = [2; 0p−1], identity covariance

rows.measure: Training and generalization misclassification rate versus training time
rows.baseline: At t = 0, generalization performance is Q(0) = 0.5; training baseline not stated.
rows.value: Generalization error first drops rapidly with training error, then goes up, although slightly, while training error continues to decrease to zero; at t = 100 early stopping is suggested for the plotted setting.
rows.note: The text describes the trajectory and gives the plotted setting; exact curve values are not stated.
rows.check: The reported error trajectory is supported by Section 4.2, but no random-label experiment establishes V1's memorization/generalization coexistence. The slight late increase in test error is not a partial instance of V1.

rows.subject: single-layer linear network
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on whitened, re-centered MNIST images of digits 1 and 7; training and generalization performance over training time.

conditions.value: artificial Gaussian white noise of −10dB; whitened and re-centered

rows.measure: Training and generalization misclassification rate versus training time
rows.value: Theoretical results and empirical simulations have an extremely close fit; figure displays training and generalization performance over time.
rows.note: The paper states the theory and simulations closely match; it does not state numerical error values in the text.
rows.check: Agreement between theoretical predictions and MNIST simulations does not measure V1. The extracted value describes prediction accuracy of the theory rather than the classifier's held-out error; no random-label comparison is performed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
